subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept this grouped update to credentialed and security-sensitive GitHub Actions after direct Codex contract review and exact-head CI complete?
rationale: The patch is mechanically narrow, but it changes executable third-party code in token, publishing, scanning, and AI-agent workflows under a protected security label, so the repository requires explicit human ownership of the boundary.

options.title: Verify and land together
options.body: Review the privileged upstream deltas, inspect the sibling Codex permission contract, and merge the grouped pins after exact-head checks finish green.

options.title: Split privileged updates
options.body: Separate token-minting, registry-publishing, security-scanning, and Codex Action bumps so each boundary can be reviewed and rolled back independently.

options.title: Pause the group
options.body: Leave the PR unmerged or close it if the grouped supply-chain review cost outweighs the benefit of these minor updates.

recommendation.title: Verify and land together
recommendation.body: Review the privileged upstream deltas, inspect the sibling Codex permission contract, and merge the grouped pins after exact-head checks finish green.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows direct ownership of release-workflow hardening and validation, which is the highest-risk changed surface.
